disclaimer: Ilm-e-Adad on Mizaj is for fun and cultural curiosity: a mirror, not a prophecy. Numbers here describe personality flavour only. Nothing on this page predicts your future, money, health, marriage or luck, and no number decides anyone's destiny. Enjoy it as heritage and a conversation starter, and make your real choices with your own judgement, effort and values.
intro:
Ilm-e-Adad, the 'knowledge of numbers', has travelled with our languages for centuries. At its heart is the Abjad system, in which every Arabic letter carries a value, from alif as 1 to ghain as 1,000, following the old sequence 'abjad, hawwaz, hutti, kalaman'. Long before modern numerals spread, scribes, scholars and poets used it every day.

Persian and Urdu poets turned it into an art called tarikh-goi: composing a chronogram, a line of verse whose letters add up to the year of a birth, a wedding, a new building or a loss. Many old inscriptions and classical diwans hide dates this way.

On Mizaj, we treat Abjad as cultural heritage and a playful mirror. Add up your name, smile at the result, and keep the conversation going.
abjad_note: Values follow Abjad-e-Qamari in abjad-hawwaz order. Urdu letters use the common convention of counting each as its base Arabic letter: پ as ب, چ as ج, ژ as ز, گ and ک as ك, ٹ as ت, ڈ as د, ڑ as ر, ں as ن, ہ ھ ة as ه, ی ے as ي, آ as ا, ؤ as و, ئ as ي. Hamza (ء) is counted as 1 here; some writers count it as 0. Short-vowel marks are ignored.
reduce_rule: Add up the value of every letter in the name, ignoring spaces and vowel marks. If the total has more than one digit, add its digits together, and repeat until you reach a single digit from 1 to 9. Exception: if any step lands on 11 or 22, stop there, because these are kept as 'master numbers'. Example: محمد = 40 + 8 + 40 + 4 = 92, and 9 + 2 = 11, a master number. علی = 70 + 30 + 10 = 110, and 1 + 1 + 0 = 2. English names work the same way with the latin table.

1.title: The Pioneer
1.planet_tradition: The Sun, in classical numerology lore
1.personality:
Number 1 is the opening move. In the old tradition it stands for beginnings, and the personality flavour matches: you like to go first, think for yourself and set your own direction. Group projects with no clear leader quietly drive you up the wall, so you often end up holding the marker at the whiteboard.

You're happiest building something with your name on it, whether that's a small business, a cricket team or a family tradition you started. People admire your confidence, even when they don't say so.

The flip side is going solo too often. Asking for help can feel like losing, but it's actually how good leaders become great ones. Let people in, and your fire spreads further.
1.strengths: Initiative is your signature. You don't wait for permission or perfect conditions; you start, adjust and keep moving. You make decisions when others stall, stay comfortable being different, and inspire people simply by showing that a new path is possible. Teams often feel braver once you step forward.
1.watch: Independence can slide into 'my way or no way'. You may brush off advice, take on too much alone, or get impatient with slower people at home and at work. Practise listening fully before replying, and remember that sharing credit doesn't shrink your achievement. Asking for help is a skill, not a weakness.
1.career_flavour: You enjoy roles where you can lead or create from scratch: running your own venture, managing a team, product design, advisory work, or freelancing with your own clients. Micromanagement drains you, so look for workplaces that reward initiative and give you clear ownership of results.

2.title: The Peacemaker
2.planet_tradition: The Moon, in classical numerology lore
2.personality:
Number 2 is about partnership. Traditionally linked with the Moon, its flavour is soft, receptive and deeply tuned in to other people. You notice moods before words, and you'd rather build a bridge than win an argument.

You're the one who quietly makes things work: patching up a fight between siblings, sending the follow-up message nobody else remembered, or sitting with a friend who just needs company. Your support often goes unseen, but people feel its absence instantly.

Your challenge is your own voice. You can bend so much for harmony that you forget what you actually want. Your kindness is real strength, and your opinions belong in the room too, even when they make things briefly uncomfortable.
2.strengths: You're a natural bridge between people. You listen carefully, read between the lines and help others feel understood. You work beautifully in partnerships and teams, bringing patience, tact and a calm presence. In tense family moments or office disagreements, your gentle diplomacy often stops small sparks from becoming fires.
2.watch: Sensitivity can turn into overthinking. You may replay a single comment for days, avoid necessary conflict, or say yes when you mean no. Practise expressing your needs early and clearly, before resentment builds. Not everyone will catch your quiet signals, so use words, kindly but plainly. Your comfort matters as much as everyone else's.
2.career_flavour: You shine in roles built on cooperation and care: counselling, teaching, HR, customer success, editing, research partnerships and collaborative design teams. You prefer supportive spaces over cut-throat competition. A respectful manager and a steady team let you do your most thoughtful work, both behind the scenes and in front.

3.title: The Storyteller
3.personality:
Number 3 is the number of expression. In the old tradition it is tied to Jupiter, and its flavour is expansive, sociable and full of colour. You light up a room with stories, jokes and an easy charm that makes strangers feel like cousins.

Words, images and ideas come naturally to you. You might be the one writing the funniest captions in the family group, designing the mehndi invitation or keeping a gathering alive with impressions of everyone's favourite drama characters.

Your challenge is focus. You can scatter your energy across ten exciting projects and finish three. Joy is your gift, but discipline is what turns talent into something lasting. Pick a few dreams, protect time for them, and watch them grow.
3.strengths: You bring optimism and creativity wherever you go. You communicate easily, cheer people up and make complex ideas sound simple and fun. Your social energy builds networks naturally, and your imagination turns ordinary plans into memorable experiences. People remember how you made them feel, which is a rare and powerful gift.
3.watch: You may joke your way around difficult emotions, or start projects enthusiastically and drop them once the excitement fades. Impulse can steer your choices more than you'd like. Try finishing one thing before beginning the next, and let close friends see your serious side. Not every silence needs filling; sometimes listening is your best performance.
3.career_flavour: Creative and communication roles suit you: content creation, marketing, media, teaching, writing, design, events and public relations. You enjoy variety and an audience. Dull routine can dim your spark, so look for roles with room to experiment. Pairing your creativity with a simple planning habit makes you remarkably effective.

4.title: The Builder
4.planet_tradition: Uranus, linked with Rahu in South Asian numerology lore
4.personality:
Number 4 is the foundation. Four walls, four seasons, four directions: its flavour is structure, stability and getting things done properly. You're the person who reads the instructions, double-checks the documents and somehow knows where the spare keys are.

You value honesty and hard work over shortcuts. People trust you because you mean what you say and finish what you start. In a world of flashy promises, your quiet reliability is a superpower.

Your challenge is flexibility. When plans change suddenly, you can feel thrown off and dig in your heels. Pakistani life, with its load-shedding, traffic and last-minute shaadi dates, keeps testing this. Leaving a little room for surprises makes your strong foundation even stronger.
4.strengths: You are dependable, thorough and patient. You turn messy ideas into working systems and see projects through to the end. Your honesty earns deep trust, and your practical skills make you the go-to person when something needs organising, fixing or managing. Families and teams lean on your steady presence without even realising it.
4.watch: Rigidity is the trap. You may resist new ideas, cling to routines that no longer work, or judge people who do things differently. Overwork can creep in quietly too. Allow yourself proper rest, try one small change at a time, and remember that a different method isn't automatically a wrong one.
4.career_flavour: You thrive in structured, detail-heavy work: engineering, accounting, project management, construction, operations, the civil service and data work. You like clear expectations and measurable progress. Chaotic workplaces frustrate you, so look for teams with good systems, or become the person who builds them.

5.title: The Wanderer
5.personality:
Number 5 sits right in the middle of 1 to 9, and its flavour is movement. Linked with quick-footed Mercury in old lore, it loves change, travel, new people and fresh ideas. You get bored easily and curious instantly.

You're adaptable in a way others envy. Drop you into a new city, a new job or a new friend group and you'll find your feet within days. You learn by doing, and you'd rather try and stumble than never try at all.

Your challenge is commitment. Routine can feel like a trap, so you may jump to the next thing before the current one has a chance to grow. Freedom feels best with a home base, so build a few anchors: one goal, one habit, a few steady people.
5.strengths: You're versatile, resourceful and quick to adapt. You connect with all kinds of people, pick up skills fast and bring energy to any team. You handle surprises calmly, often better than the planners do. Your sense of adventure inspires friends to step outside their comfort zones and try something new.
5.watch: Restlessness can scatter you. You may abandon plans midway, overcommit to exciting offers, or get impatient with slow processes like university admissions and paperwork. Impulsive decisions often follow boredom. Before saying yes to the next shiny thing, ask whether it fits the bigger picture you actually want.
5.career_flavour: Variety-heavy roles suit you: sales, travel and tourism, journalism, marketing, freelancing, advisory roles, aviation and events. You enjoy movement, new faces and quick decisions. Desk-bound routine drains you, so look for roles with change built in, or balance steady work with side projects that keep you curious.

6.title: The Nurturer
6.personality:
Number 6 is the number of home and heart. Linked with Venus in the old tradition, its flavour is warmth, beauty and responsibility for the people you love. You're the one who makes a house feel like a home.

You notice when guests need more chai, when a friend needs a call, and when the drawing room needs fresh flowers before the rishta visit. Harmony matters to you, and you put real effort into creating it.

Your challenge is over-giving. You may take responsibility for everyone's happiness and feel hurt when your care isn't noticed. Your love is generous, but it also needs boundaries. Looking after yourself is part of looking after your people, not a betrayal of them.
6.strengths: You are loyal, nurturing and dependable. You create beautiful, welcoming spaces and bring people together. Others trust you with their worries because you listen with care. You have a natural sense of fairness and duty, and you usually step up when family or friends need practical or emotional support.
6.watch: Caring can slip into controlling or worrying too much. You may give unasked-for advice, feel responsible for everyone's choices, or quietly resent being taken for granted. Practise letting people make their own mistakes. Say no sometimes, rest without guilt, and remember that love doesn't require constant sacrifice.
6.career_flavour: Caring and creative roles suit you: teaching, nursing, counselling, interior design, hospitality, fashion and community work. You want work that feels meaningful and genuinely helps people. Cut-throat cultures drain you, so look for teams where kindness is valued alongside results.

7.title: The Seeker
7.planet_tradition: Neptune, linked with Ketu in South Asian numerology lore
7.personality:
Number 7 is the thinker's number. It turns up everywhere, from the seven days of the week to the seven colours of the rainbow, and its flavour is depth, reflection and quiet curiosity. You want to know what lies beneath the surface.

You're comfortable in your own company. A long walk, a good book or one deep conversation recharges you more than a crowded dholki. People may call you mysterious, but you're simply selective about who sees your inner world.

Your challenge is connection. You can retreat into your head, overanalyse feelings and assume others won't understand you. Letting a few trusted people in, even imperfectly, keeps your wisdom from turning into isolation. Your questions are valuable, so share them.
7.strengths: You think deeply and observe carefully. You can research, analyse and understand complex ideas that others skim past. Your intuition is sharp, and your advice is considered rather than rushed. People value your calm, honest perspective, especially when they need someone who won't simply tell them what they want to hear.
7.watch: You may withdraw when stressed, become overly critical of others, or doubt people's intentions. Overthinking can freeze decisions. Try sharing your thoughts before they're perfectly formed, and stay connected even during your quiet seasons. Not every question has a final answer; sometimes trust and action matter more than certainty.
7.career_flavour: Depth-focused roles suit you: research, science, data analysis, writing, psychology, academia, software and investigative work. You need quiet time to think and dislike shallow busywork. Look for places that respect expertise and give you room to dig deep, and team up with people who help you share your findings.

8.title: The Powerhouse
8.personality:
Number 8 is about strength and structure. Linked with patient Saturn in the old tradition, its flavour is ambition, resilience and a serious approach to responsibility. You think about the long game, and you're not afraid of hard work.

You're often the one people turn to when decisions need making. Whether it's helping with a family business, leading a university society or untangling a complicated situation, you bring authority and steadiness. Setbacks rarely keep you down for long.

Your challenge is balance. You can tie your self-worth to achievement and forget to rest, laugh or share your feelings. Strength includes softness too. Celebrate effort, not just results, and let the people around you see the person behind the plans.
8.strengths: You're determined, organised and resilient. You take charge in tough situations, plan for the long term and stay focused under pressure. People trust your judgement in practical matters. You have a talent for turning ideas into structures that last, and you rarely give up on goals you truly care about.
8.watch: Ambition can become workaholism, and confidence can slide into control. You may be hard on yourself and others, or struggle to show vulnerability. Watch for stress building quietly. Schedule real rest, delegate without micromanaging, and remember that the people who love you want your presence, not just your provision.
8.career_flavour: Leadership and management roles suit you: business, finance, law, administration, the civil service, property and operations. You like authority, clear goals and measurable growth. Ethical leadership is your sweet spot. Find mentors who model balance, and build teams strong enough that you don't carry everything alone.

9.title: The Humanitarian
9.personality:
Number 9 completes the cycle from 1 to 9, and its flavour is big-hearted and wise beyond its years. Linked with fiery Mars in old lore, it carries both passion and compassion: you feel strongly, and you want to make things better.

You care about people you've never met. You're the one organising the flood relief drive, giving quietly in Ramadan or standing up for someone being treated unfairly. Your circle is wide, and your heart is wider.

Your challenge is letting go. You can carry everyone's pain, struggle with endings and feel let down when the world doesn't match your ideals. You can't fix everything alone. Caring for yourself keeps your generosity alive for the long run.
9.strengths: You're compassionate, generous and broad-minded. You connect with people from every background and inspire others to do good. Your passion fuels causes, creative work and community projects. You have a natural wisdom about life's ups and downs, and people often come to you for perspective when things feel overwhelming.
9.watch: Idealism can lead to disappointment, and generosity can leave you drained. You may struggle to say no, hold onto past hurts, or flare up when you see injustice. Choose your battles, set boundaries around your time, and allow endings gracefully. Not every person or cause is yours to rescue.
9.career_flavour: Purpose-driven roles suit you: social work, NGOs, teaching, healthcare support, the arts, law, international development and creative writing. You need work that feels meaningful beyond a salary. Look for organisations whose values match yours, and protect your energy so your passion doesn't burn out.

11.title: The Visionary
11.planet_tradition: The Moon, shared with number 2 (1+1) in numerology lore
11.personality:
11 is the first 'master number', kept whole instead of being reduced to 2. Its flavour is number 2's sensitivity turned up to full volume: intuitive, idealistic and quietly electric. You often sense things before you can explain them.

You may feel slightly different from the people around you: more tuned in, more affected by atmosphere, more drawn to big questions about meaning and purpose. Friends come to you for perspective, and your words can land with surprising impact.

Your challenge is nerves. All that sensitivity can tip into worry, self-doubt or overwhelm. Grounding habits like good sleep, routine, prayer or time outdoors help your bright inner signal come through clearly instead of as static.
11.strengths: You inspire people. Your intuition picks up unspoken feelings and hidden possibilities, and you can express ideas in ways that move others. You're idealistic, creative and empathetic, often seeing what a person or project could become. When you trust yourself, your quiet confidence can lift an entire room.
11.watch: High sensitivity can make criticism feel enormous and decisions feel heavy. You may swing between big dreams and self-doubt, or absorb stress from others. Build routines that steady you, choose your inner circle carefully, and turn ideas into small practical steps so your vision doesn't stay in the clouds.
11.career_flavour: Inspiring, meaningful roles suit you: teaching, counselling, writing, the arts, design, public speaking and community work. You want your work to matter. Pure numbers-and-targets environments may drain you. Pair your vision with a practical teammate who helps turn inspiration into plans that actually happen.

22.title: The Master Builder
22.planet_tradition: Uranus and Rahu, shared with number 4 (2+2) in numerology lore
22.personality:
22 is the second master number, kept whole instead of being reduced to 4. Its flavour combines 4's brick-by-brick discipline with a much bigger vision. You don't just dream about change; you think about the systems, budgets and timelines needed to make it real.

People often see you as mature beyond your years. You might be planning a community project while friends are still choosing a café, or quietly turning a small idea into something that helps many people.

Your challenge is pressure. Big vision brings big expectations, and you can feel crushed by your own standards. Break goals into smaller pieces, celebrate progress and let others share the load. Even the grandest buildings rise one floor at a time.
22.strengths: You combine vision with practicality, which is rare. You can plan large projects, organise people and resources, and stay disciplined over the long haul. Others trust you to turn ideas into reality. Your steady leadership, patience and sense of responsibility make you a natural anchor for teams, families and communities.
22.watch: You may set impossibly high standards, overwork, or feel frustrated when others don't share your urgency. Fear of failure can make you rigid or controlling. Allow room for imperfection, rest without guilt, and remember that impact grows through collaboration. You don't need to build the whole city alone.
22.career_flavour: Large-scale, impact-driven roles suit you: engineering, urban planning, public policy, project leadership, social enterprise, technology and the civil service. You enjoy building systems that outlast you. Small, aimless work frustrates you, so look for long-term missions and people who balance your intensity with lightness.

birth_number_intro: Your life-path number, or birth number, comes from your date of birth rather than your name. Add every digit of the full date: 14-08-1998 becomes 1+4+0+8+1+9+9+8 = 40, then 4+0 = 4. Keep 11 and 22 whole as master numbers. Read it as a second mirror next to your name number, purely for fun and reflection.
